title: fix(plugin-detail): the related-list renderer's props type refuses a misspelled key again (objectui#9963)
body:
Fixes #9963
Clause-②: no

`RecordRelatedListRendererProps` refuses a misspelled key again, at every read in the
`record:related_list` renderer, and keeps exactly the looseness objectstack#6953 needs.

⚠️ **Type parameters are spelled with SQUARE brackets in this body** (`Record[string, any]`,
`Pick[...]`), because the GitHub body sanitizer eats angle-bracket-shaped fragments, even
inside backticks. The source spells them the normal way.

## The defect, reproduced before it was repaired

On `origin/main` at `6099dd87`, the renderer's `schema` member was the mirror
`RecordRelatedListComponentProps` (with `objectName` made optional) intersected with
`Record[string, any]`, and the props interface also carried `[k: string]: any`. The new
pin file `record-related-list.propsRefusal-9963.test.tsx` was compiled against that
unchanged renderer (`tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`, before the fix): **8 errors, all in the
new file**:

- the misspelled read `schema.relationshipValueFeild`: `@ts-expect-error` UNUSED (TS2578),
  i.e. the misspelling type-checked;
- the exact-key-set leg (`keyof Schema` equal to the mirror's keys plus `dataSource`): TS2344,
  because an index signature makes `keyof` read `string | number`;
- `Schema['dataSource']` equal to the gate's `ElementDataSourceConfig`: TS2344 (it was `any`);
- the host-props key-set leg: TS2344; the misspelled host prop `props.classname`: TS2578;
- the three cast-read keys written into a typed `schema` literal: TS2578 x3 (admitted).

Every control in the same command stayed green: the SAME misspelling through the mirror
(no index signature) was refused, and the authoring shape, the full binding and a literal
carrying all 12 mirror members all type-checked.

## The minimal honest shape — every read enumerated with the checker

A TypeScript program over the renderer walked every property access whose base is
`schema` (bare or through a cast) or `props`, and classified each key with
`getPropertiesOfType` on the mirror (real members only; an index signature does not count):

| class | keys (reads) | how read |
|---|---|---|
| (a) declared on the mirror | `add` (4), `aria` (1), `columns` (2), `filter` (1), `limit` (3), `objectName` (1), `relationshipField` (3), `relationshipValueField` (1), `sort` (1), `title` (1) | un-cast |
| (b) the objectstack#6953 authoring shape | `dataSource` | read by `ElementDataSourceGate` (`useElementDataSource`), never by the body; `objectName` optional because the gate binds it |
| (c) other | `requiredPermissions` (2), `enforceFieldSecurity` (1), `redactFields` (2) | through `(schema as any)` casts |

(c) are real reads, not dead code. objectui#8649 ruled them "declared by no block the
contract maps" and routed them to the producer; `detailRendererUndeclaredKeys-8649.test.ts`
ledgers them. Their **reads are untouched**, because each goes through its own cast. What
the narrowing now refuses is a **typed** call site writing one of them into a `schema`
literal (TS2353). ⛔ They are NOT re-admitted: no index signature, no new member.

Two mirror members, `showViewAll` and `actions`, are read by nothing in this renderer.
That is noted below under Acceptance notes and not acted on.

**What the registry forwards: measured, not read off the code.** A throwaway probe (not
committed) rendered a real `SchemaRenderer` over the real registration with the entry
swapped for a spy. It captured the component's props for a node carrying `id`,
`className`, `relationshipField`, `dataSource`, `aria` and `properties`:

`aria`, `className`, `data-obj-id`, `data-obj-type`, `disabled`, `id`, `limit`, `properties`,
`relationshipField`, `title`, plus `schema` (whose keys were `aria, className, dataSource,
id, limit, properties, relationshipField, title, type`).

The component reads only `schema`, `className`, and the three keys `splitDesigner`
destructures (`style`, `data-obj-id`, `data-obj-type`). The registry's call does not bind
this declaration: the registration goes through `ComponentRenderer[T = any]` on a
`Registry[any]`. So the declared host props are the ones read, and what is forwarded
and never read is not declared.

**The shape now:** the mirror minus `objectName`, plus `objectName` optional, plus
`{ dataSource?: ElementDataSourceConfig }`. The props are `schema`, `className`, `style`,
`data-obj-id` and `data-obj-type`. `ElementDataSourceConfig` is the gate's own existing
export from `@object-ui/core`, a peer dependency already. Measured on the built
`dist/renderers/record-related-list.d.ts`: it imports `ElementDataSourceConfig` from
`@object-ui/core` and exports no new type. ⇒ `Clause-②: no` holds.

## After the repair (HEAD `979764a1`)

The same pins are green. The `@ts-expect-error` directives fire for the right reason. A
throwaway copy with the directives stripped reported:

- TS2551 "Did you mean 'relationshipValueField'?" on the schema read;
- TS2551 "Did you mean 'className'?" on the host prop;
- TS2353 on each of the three (c) literals.

## Ablation, with on-disk proof, both legs restored

Both legs were run through `ablation-replace.mjs` (a literal anchor that must hit, blob
hashes, restore by `git checkout HEAD`), then `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`:

- **Leg A: put `& Record[string, any]` back on `schema`.** The anchor went 1 to 0 and the
  replacement 0 to 1. The blob went `b97d2f7c2640` to `38afd1d37cfd`, and an on-disk grep
  counted 1. tsc then gave exactly **5 errors**: the misspelled read (TS2578), the key-set
  leg (TS2344) and the three (c) legs (TS2578). The authoring-shape, full-binding,
  all-mirror-members, `dataSource`-type, `objectName` and host-props legs stayed green.
  The mirror control stayed green too. Restored: blob `b97d2f7c2640` equals HEAD, and
  `git diff HEAD` is empty.
- **Leg B: put `[k: string]: any` back on the props interface.** tsc gave exactly **2
  errors**: the host key-set leg (TS2344) and the misspelled host prop (TS2578).
  Everything else stayed green. Restored: blob equals HEAD, and `git diff HEAD` is empty.
  ⚠️ The first leg-B attempt was refused by the tool before anything ran. Its replacement
  contained the anchor, so the anchor count could not fall. Nothing was measured on it;
  the retry used a non-overlapping replacement.

## Consumers

- `@object-ui/plugin-detail` `type-check` at HEAD `979764a1` (both `tsc --noEmit` and
  `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`): **exit 0, 0 errors**. The test project compiles 201 test files
  (`--listFiles`: 200 tracked plus the new one). That includes every
  `RecordRelatedListRenderer` JSX site in `src/__tests__/` and `src/renderers/__tests__/`,
  so no existing call site broke. The one in `record-blocks.requiredPermissions-gate.test.tsx`
  passes its schema `as any`.
- **Every importer's `type-check`, at HEAD `979764a1`**, after building their union
  dependency closure (35 workspace packages). The eight workspace packages that depend on
  `@object-ui/plugin-detail` are `plugin-calendar`, `plugin-gantt`, `plugin-grid`,
  `plugin-kanban`, `plugin-tree`, `example-console-starter`, `app-shell` and `console`.
  Each ran `type-check`, and each log echoes the script name. **All 8 exited 0 with 0
  errors.** No importer broke, so nothing was widened back.
- The objectui#9475 ledger leg `_MisspellingIsStillAdmittedHere` went red, as it was
  written to do on the day this intersection narrowed. Its re-derivation and its mirror
  control moved to the new pin file, and that file's header was updated.

## Census the card left NOT MEASURED

An AST walk ran over every non-test source of `packages/plugin-detail/src` at
`6099dd87`, 57 files and 44 declarations named `*Props`. Enumeration and reads both came
from that one commit. **10** declarations carry an `any` string index, on the interface
and/or folded into `schema`. `record-related-list.tsx` is among them, as the lit control;
34 carry none. So **9 other renderers** carry the shape:

- 4 with the exact mirror-intersection form: `record-chatter`, `record-details`,
  `record-highlights`, `record-path`;
- 4 with `[k: string]: any` inside an inline `schema` literal: `record-activity`,
  `record-history`, `record-quick-actions`, `record-reference-rail`;
- 1 with the outer index only: `record-alert`.

All 9 carry the outer `[k: string]: any`.

The census reads syntax, so it was followed by a type-level reading at HEAD `979764a1`.
A throwaway file, never committed and removed under a trap, put `@ts-expect-error` on
one misspelled DECLARED `schema` member per renderer, and on a misspelled `className`
per renderer:

- **8 of the 9 admit the schema misspelling.** `record-alert` refuses it, because its
  `schema` carries no index; that refusal is what makes the other column a reading.
- **All 9 admit the host-prop misspelling.**
- `record-related-list` refused both. It is the lit control.

⛔ None of the 9 is touched here; they go to the report as findings.

## Verification (HEAD `979764a1`)

- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-detail/` (repo root): **200 files passed, 1
  skipped (201); 2005 tests passed, 8 skipped**.
- The dependency closure was built before any type reading (`pnpm --filter
  '@object-ui/plugin-detail^...' build`), so the pins read rebuilt `.d.ts` files.
- Gates, all exit 0: `check:control-bytes`, `check:new-line-citations` (0 new
  citations), `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` (1 changeset declared),
  `check:element-data-source-declaration`, `check:component-surface-parity`,
  `check:handler-key-reads`, `check:comment-mask-corpus`, `check:test-path-roots`,
  `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit`, `check:vi-mock-override-shape`,
  `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:phantom-deps`,
  `check:installed-pin-claims`, `check:published-tsconfig-exclude`.
- NOT MEASURED: `check:sdui-registration-pins` (it needs a console bundle, exit 2
  PREREQUISITE) and `check:readme-exports` (it needs every package built, and its
  population collapsed). Neither reads a file this diff touches: no registration array,
  README or export moved.
- eslint, narrowed and declared. The population is the three touched `.ts`/`.tsx` files,
  and `--format json` counted 3 files linted, **0 errors**. The renderer went from 24 to
  22 warnings, the two `any` removed. The narrowing is safe: `eslint.config.js` enables no
  type-aware linting (0 occurrences of `projectService` or `project:`, against 9 each of
  `rules:` and `files:`), so no rule can read a file this diff did not touch. The
  repository-wide `pnpm lint` is CI's run.
- NOT MEASURED: remote CI. This is handed over before CI converges.

## Changeset

`@object-ui/plugin-detail: minor`. A published props type narrows: TypeScript callers
that wrote a key outside the declared set now fail to compile. `major` is banned by this
repo's version policy, and the changeset body states the breaking semantics. The runtime
is unchanged: `SchemaRenderer` forwards exactly what it did, and nothing the renderer
reads moved.

## Acceptance notes

- **`showViewAll` and `actions` are declared and published but read by nothing.** Both are
  declared on the spec's `RecordRelatedListProps` ("Show View All link to see all related
  records", "Action IDs available for related records"), on the mirror, and as registry
  inputs. This renderer reads neither and hands neither to `RelatedList`. `RelatedList`
  does draw a View All link, but only when an `onViewAll` prop is passed, and this block
  never passes one. This card keeps both admitted, because they are mirror members;
  whether they are live is a separate question, handed to the report as a finding.
- The wrapper still hands the bound schema to the body as `schema={bound as any}`. Both
  sides already carry the same type, so the cast is inert. It was left alone because it is
  not a read and the change is out of this card's question.
- No doc names this TypeScript props type. A grep for `RecordRelatedListRenderer` over
  `content/docs` and the package README finds 0 hits; the lit control, the same grep for
  `record:related_list`, finds several. So no doc moves.
- Open PR objectui#10279 edits the sibling `record-blocks.requiredPermissions-gate.test.tsx`.
  Its related-list site passes `schema as any`, so there is no textual or type overlap
  with this narrowing.
